notes: Also $100000 property damage per occurrence; applies to municipalities and counties; notice 6 months to municipal clerk (12 months to county commission); punitive bar is Ala. Code 6-11-26 (not in chart)
No damage caps; no notice-of-claim requirement (charter notice provisions impliedly prohibited per Johnson v. City of Fairbanks); discretionary-function immunity only
Ariz. Const. art. II sec. 31 forbids any law limiting damages for death or injury; notice of claim within 180 days (A.R.S. 12-821.01); suit within 1 year

notes: No statutory dollar cap but political subdivisions are immune from negligence liability except to the extent of liability insurance (Ark. Code 21-9-301); minimum motor-vehicle liability insurance $25000 per person / $50000 per occurrence / $25000 property (21-9-303); no notice requirement
No cap; claim must be presented within 6 months for injury/property (1 year other claims) under Gov. Code 911.2; punitive barred by Gov. Code 818
source: Cal. Gov. Code 815 et seq.; 818; 911.2; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: CGIA caps inflation-adjusted every 4 years: $350000/$990000 pre-2018 (chart shows $350000/$900000); $424000/$1195000 for 2022-2025; $505000/$1421000 for injuries 2026-2030; punitive bar is C.R.S. 24-10-114(4) (not in chart); notice 182 days (24-10-109)
source: C.R.S. 24-10-114; 24-10-109; Colorado Special Districts Pool notice Jan 2026 (csdplwcp.specialdistrict.org/new-cgia-limits-for-2026); MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: No cap; chart lists written notice to municipal clerk within 6 months and 90-day notice for highway/sidewalk defect claims (13a-149); 2-year limitation

$300000 for all claims from a single occurrence unless the political subdivision carries insurance above that (then policy limit); liability only for the three 4012 exceptions (vehicles/equipment; public buildings; pollutant discharge); municipalities may set notice by ordinance up to 1 year; statewide transit (DART/DTC) is a state agency under the State Tort Claims subchapter not this cap
No cap; written notice to the Mayor within 6 months (D.C. Code 12-309); police report sufficient; WMATA is an interstate compact agency outside D.C. law

$200000 per person / $300000 per incident (F.S. 768.28(5)) for state agencies and subdivisions including counties and municipalities; excess recoverable only by legislative claim bill; notice within 3 years (2 for wrongful death); 2026 HB 145 ($350000/$500000 effective 10/1/2026) reported vetoed by the Governor June 2026 (secondary source; formal veto record not confirmed); punitive barred by 768.28(5)
source: F.S. 768.28(5) and (6); floridacourtrules.com HB 145 veto note (2026); MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: Caps apply ONLY to motor-vehicle claims: $500000 per person / $700000 per occurrence / $50000 property (O.C.G.A. 36-92-2); otherwise municipalities immune except to the extent liability insurance is purchased (36-33-1); notice 6 months to municipality (12 months county); MARTA governed by its own act (not addressed in chart)
No cap; counties have no sovereign immunity; notice of claim within 2 years (Haw. Rev. Stat. 46-72)

$500000 per occurrence for political subdivisions unless insurance in excess purchased or conduct willful/reckless (Idaho Code 6-926); notice 180 days (6-906); punitive barred (6-918); political subdivision definition (6-902) covers public corporations
No cap; no notice of claim (1-year limitation under 745 ILCS 10/8-101); punitive barred (10/2-102); CTA has its own 6-month notice rule (70 ILCS 3605/41) not in chart

$700000 per person (for causes after 1/1/2008) and $5000000 per occurrence (I.C. 34-13-3-4); notice to political subdivision within 180 days (34-13-3-8); political subdivision includes public transportation corporations
No damage caps; no notice of claim (2-year limitation under I.C.A. 670.5); punitive barred (670.4)

$500000 per occurrence (K.S.A. 75-6105); written notice to clerk/governing body required before suit (12-105b) with 120-day waiting period but no separate filing deadline shorter than the limitation period; municipality definition covers political subdivisions and public corporations

No statutory dollar cap on cities under the Claims Against Local Governments Act (KRS 65.2001-65.2006); the chart's $200000/$350000 figure is the state Board of Claims cap (now KRS 49.040: $250000 per claim) which does not govern cities; counties retain sovereign immunity; punitive barred (Phelps v. Louisville Water Co.); 90-day notice applies to street/sidewalk defect claims against cities
source: KRS 65.2001-65.2006; KRS 49.040; KRS 411.110; law.justia.com KRS 49.040 (2025); ij.org Kentucky profile; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: $500000 per person cap on general (non-economic) damages for injury or death (La. $400000 per occurrence (14 M.R.S. 8105); employee personal liability $10000; immunity waived up to insurance limits if entity otherwise immune (8116); notice 180 days (8107); punitive barred (8105)

LGTCA: $400000 per individual claim / $800000 per occurrence excluding interest (Cts. & Jud. Proc. 5-303); notice within 1 year (5-304); local government may not be liable for punitive damages (5-303(c)); the Maryland Transit Administration is a state unit under the Maryland Tort Claims Act ($400000 per claimant) and WMATA is an interstate compact so neither is under the LGTCA cap
source: Md. Code Cts. & Jud. Proc. 5-303; 5-304; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: $100000 per plaintiff cap with no per-occurrence aggregate (M.G.L. c. 258 sec. 2); MBTA claims expressly NOT subject to the $100000 limit; presentment within 2 years; no punitive damages or prejudgment interest; regional transit authorities not addressed in chart
source: M.G.L. c. 258 secs. 2 and 4; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: No cap; broad governmental-function immunity with six statutory exceptions (highways; vehicles; public buildings; proprietary functions; medical care; sewage events); notice 120 days for highway-defect claims (M.C.L. 691.1404); punitive generally not recoverable absent statute (case law)

$500000 per claimant / $1500000 per occurrence for claims after 7/1/2009 (Minn. Stat. 466.04); 2x limits for hazardous-substance releases; if insurance purchased the policy limits are the maximum; no punitive damages; notice 180 days (466.05); municipality definition covers public authorities and special districts

$500000 for all claims from a single occurrence for all governmental entities including political subdivisions (Miss. Code 11-46-15); insurance limits may exceed the statutory amount (11-46-16); no punitive damages; notice must be served at least 90 days BEFORE suit (11-46-11) and suit within 1 year

Statutory base $300000 per person / $2000000 per occurrence (RSMo 537.610) is inflation-adjusted annually by the Dept. of Commerce and Insurance: 2025 = $517306 / $3448710; 2026 = $532148 / $3547658; no punitive damages (537.610.3); city-specific 90-day notice statutes (e.g. RSMo 82.210 for larger cities) not in chart; Bi-State Development and KCATA are interstate compact agencies so coverage is unclear
source: RSMo 537.610; insurance.mo.gov Sovereign Immunity Limits by Year (2026); MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: $750000 per claim / $1500000 per occurrence (Mont. Code 2-9-108); insurer may endorse higher coverage; punitive/exemplary barred (2-9-105); claim must be presented to clerk/secretary before suit with 120-day decision period but chart gives no fixed filing deadline

$1000000 per person / $5000000 per occurrence (Neb. Rev. Stat. 13-926); notice within 1 year and suit within 2 years (13-919); PSTCA applied to the Transit Authority of the City of Omaha (chart cites Great N. Ins. Co. v. Transit Auth. 2021); punitive bar reflects the Nebraska constitutional rule against punitive damages (chart silent)

Per-claimant cap only (no per-occurrence aggregate): $200000 exclusive of interest (NRS 41.035(1); chart's $100000 is stale); no exemplary or punitive damages; claim filed with governing body within 2 years (41.036) but filing is not a condition precedent to suit

$275000 per person / $925000 per occurrence for bodily injury or property damage (RSA 507-B:4); notice within 60 days of discovery (507-B:7); 3-year limitation; punitive bar reflects RSA 507:16 general bar (chart silent)

No dollar caps; pain-and-suffering recoverable only for permanent loss of bodily function/disfigurement/dismemberment with medical expenses over $3600; no punitive damages (N.J.S.A. 59:9-2); notice within 90 days (59:8-8); NJ Transit is a state instrumentality under the same Act

Per person: $400000 for all damages other than medical expenses and real property plus up to $300000 past and future medical expenses plus $200000 per parcel of real property; $750000 aggregate per occurrence for non-property damages (NMSA 41-4-19 as amended 2007 for torts after 7/1/2008); no evidence found of amendment through 2024; no punitive damages; written notice to local public body within 90 days (41-4-16)

No cap; notice of claim within 90 days (Gen. Mun. Law 50-e); suit within 1 year and 90 days (50-i); punitive barred against municipalities by case law (chart cites Wang v. N.Y. State Dep't of Health); MTA/NYCTA follow the same 90-day notice rule and have no cap
source: N.Y. Gen. Mun. Law 50-e; 50-i; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: No statutory cap for local governments; governmental immunity waived only to the extent of liability insurance or risk-pool coverage (N.C.G.S. 153A-435 counties; 160A-485 cities); the chart's $1000000 per occurrence is the State Tort Claims Act cap (143-299.2) which applies only to the State and to cities over 500000 (Charlotte) that elect into it; punitive not allowed absent statute; no notice requirement (cities may adopt their own)

Current N.D.C.C. 32-12.1-03(2): $500000 per person / $2000000 per occurrence regardless of number of political subdivisions involved (chart's $250000/$1000000 is stale); political subdivision may not be liable for punitive or exemplary damages (same subsection); insurance or self-insurance pool may cover excess; no notice requirement; 3-year limitation (32-12.1-10)
source: N.D.C.C. 32-12.1-03(2); 32-12.1-05; 32-12.1-10 (ndlegis.gov Century Code ch. 32-12.1 current); MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: No limit on economic damages; non-economic damages capped at $250000 per plaintiff (R.C. 2744.05(C)); medical malpractice against political subdivisions $350000 per person / $500000 per occurrence (non-catastrophic) and $500000 / $1000000 (catastrophic); no punitive damages (2744.05(A)); collateral-source offset; no notice of claim (2-year limitation 2744.04); regional transit authorities are political subdivisions (2744.01(F))

51 O.S. 154(A): $25000 property; $125000 per claimant for other loss; $175000 per claimant if the defendant is the State or a city/county with population 300000 or more (chart lists only $175000); $200000 for medical negligence; $1000000 for all claims from a single occurrence; no punitive damages (154(C)); notice within 1 year (156(B)); the $125000 tier is from a secondary source (legalclarity.org) because OSCN blocked retrieval of the statute text
source: 51 O.S. 154; 156; legalclarity.org GTCA summary; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: Local public body limits (ORS 30.272) adjusted each July 1 by the State Court Administrator (max 3% per year): 7/1/2024-6/30/2025 = $855200 / $1710200; 7/1/2025-6/30/2026 = $879200 / $1758300; 7/1/2026-6/30/2027 = $902700 / $1805300; property damage $148100 / $740300 for 2026-27; state limits are higher (ORS 30.271); no punitive damages (30.269); notice 180 days (1 year for death) under 30.275; mass transit districts such as TriMet are local public bodies
source: ORS 30.272; 30.269; 30.275; courts.oregon.gov Tort Claims page and Table of Liability Limits (2026); MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: Local agencies: no per-person limit; $500000 aggregate for all damages arising from the same cause of action (42 Pa.C.S. 8553); pain and suffering only for permanent loss of bodily function/disfigurement/dismemberment with medical expenses over $1500; punitive not among recoverable damage types; notice within 6 months (42 Pa.C.S. 5522); unchanged since 1978 and upheld by the PA Supreme Court; 2024-25 bills (SB 1300; SB 383) to raise it had not been enacted as of search; SEPTA is a Commonwealth agency subject instead to the $250000/$1000000 sovereign cap (8528) while county/regional authorities (e.g. Pittsburgh Regional Transit) are local agencies
source: 42 Pa.C.S. 8553; 8528; 5522; Lamb McErlane and White and Williams alerts (2023-24); PA LBFC report 2022; MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: $100000 limit on tort damages against political subdivisions (R.I.G.L. 9-31-3) but the limit does not apply when the subdivision was engaged in a proprietary function or has agreed to indemnify the federal government; chart does not specify per-claimant vs per-occurrence basis; 3-year limitation; RIPTA is a state authority not addressed in chart

$300000 per person / $600000 per occurrence (S.C. Code 15-78-120); $1200000 per occurrence for government physicians/dentists; no punitive damages; notice is not a prerequisite (2-year limitation; 3 years if verified claim filed)

Chart lists no damage cap but sovereign immunity is waived only to the extent of risk-pool or liability insurance coverage (SDCL 21-32A-1) so coverage limits act as the effective ceiling; written notice within 180 days; suit within 1 year

GTLA minimum insurance limits for actions arising after 7/1/2007: $300000 per person / $700000 per occurrence / $100000 property (Tenn. source: Tenn. Code 29-20-403; 29-20-311; 29-20-305; codes.findlaw.com 29-20-403 (current as of 1/2/2024); MWL chart 2/14/22

notes: Municipalities: $250000 per person / $500000 per occurrence bodily injury and $100000 per occurrence property (CPRC 101.023(c)); counties and all other units of local government including transit authorities: $100000 per person / $300000 per occurrence / $100000 property (101.023(b)); no punitive damages (101.024); written notice within 6 months (101.101) with shorter charter periods allowed; school/junior college districts waived only for motor vehicles
source: Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 101.023; 101.024; 101.101; MWL chart 2/14/22

No statutory cap for local governments; counties retain full sovereign immunity; cities and towns liable for proprietary (not governmental) functions; the Virginia Tort Claims Act $100000 cap (8.01-195.3) covers the Commonwealth and transportation districts so transit district commissions may fall under that state cap; chart lists 6-month notice (cities/towns: Va. Code 8.01-222)

No cap; local governmental entities liable for governmental and proprietary acts to the same extent as a person (RCW 4.96.010); standard claim form must be filed and 60 days must elapse before suit (4.96.020) but no separate deadline shorter than the limitation period; punitive barred by Washington common law absent statute (chart silent)

No limit on economic damages; non-economic damages limited to $500000 per occurrence (W. Va. Code 29-12A-7(b); chart cites 29-12A-6); punitive barred (29-12A-7(a)); Act applies only to political subdivisions not the State; 2-year limitation; no notice of claim

General per-claimant cap of $50000 against any political corporation or governmental subdivision with no per-occurrence aggregate (Wis. $250000 per claimant / $500000 per occurrence (Wyo.
